prompt: How many input tokens did the three requests of the uncached run carry in total?
Why did each request carry about 2,350 tokens before any of the conversation?

choices.text: Because labllm pads every request
choices.why: labllm counts what it receives.

choices.text: The tools and the system prompt with the policies are sent every time
choices.why: Right. The API keeps nothing between requests.

choices.text: Because the model's answer is counted as input
choices.why: The answer is output, 93 tokens in all.

choices.text: Because of the cache
choices.why: This run had no cache.

prompt: Why did request 3 take about 3,200 ms when requests 1 and 2 took about 600?

choices.text: It carried the most input tokens
choices.why: labllm spends no time on input; the difference was 41 tokens.

choices.text: Because search_help ran during it
choices.why: Tools run between requests, not during them.

choices.text: Because the provider was overloaded and retried it once, without the program noticing
choices.why: No retry happened in this run.

choices.text: It wrote the 75-token answer
choices.why: Right. 200 ms plus 75 × 40 ms.

prompt: What does streaming change for the person waiting?

choices.text: The total time, which falls by half
choices.why: The work is the same; only when the first words appear changes.

choices.text: When the first words appear
choices.why: Right. After the time to first token, not after the whole answer.

choices.text: The number of tokens
choices.why: The same tokens are written.

choices.text: The price per token, because streamed tokens are billed at a lower rate by most providers
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

prompt: How many milliseconds did the whole run take with scripted-mini?
What did switching to scripted-mini not change?

choices.text: The time to write the answer
choices.why: It fell from 3,208 ms to 957.

choices.text: The total time
choices.why: It fell to 1,939 ms.

choices.text: The tokens: 7,440 in and 93 out
choices.why: Right. Speed changed; the shape of the bill did not.

choices.text: The time per output token, which stays at 40 ms for every model of the lab
choices.why: It is 10 ms for scripted-mini.

prompt: In the second cached run, what happened to the prefix on request 1?

choices.text: It was read from the cache, within its 300 seconds
choices.why: Right. No write at all in that run.

choices.text: It was written again
choices.why: That was the first run.

choices.text: It was left out of the request
choices.why: The request still carries it; the provider bills it as a read.

choices.text: It was ignored
choices.why: It was read, 2,347 tokens.

prompt: Why did --stamp make caching worse than no caching?

choices.text: Because timestamps are not allowed in system prompts
choices.why: They are allowed; they change the prefix.

choices.text: Because it made the prompt much longer, pushing it past the context window
choices.why: It added a few tokens.

choices.text: Because labllm forgets the cache when a run ends
choices.why: The second cached run read it from the first.

choices.text: The front of the prefix changed, so every request wrote it again
choices.why: Right. 7,074 tokens written and none read; writes cost more than plain input.

hint: A change near the front breaks everything after it.

prompt: What did the reply with max_tokens=8 come back as?

choices.text: An error, raised by the SDK
choices.why: The request succeeded.

choices.text: Half a sentence, with stop_reason max_tokens
choices.why: Right. A program must check stop_reason.

choices.text: The full answer, since the limit only applies to tool calls and not to text
choices.why: It applies to every reply.

choices.text: An empty reply
choices.why: It held 8 tokens of text.

prompt: A prompt longer than the model's window got HTTP status ___ before any work was done.
Why did the call with two 529 failures succeed?

choices.text: Because labllm ignored the configuration
choices.why: The log shows 529 529 200.

choices.text: Because 529 is not an error
choices.why: It is the status for an overloaded provider.

choices.text: The SDK retried twice on its own
choices.why: Right. With three failures it gave up and raised OverloadedError.

choices.text: Because limits.py catches the error and calls again until the provider answers, without a limit
choices.why: limits.py makes one call; the retries were the SDK's.

prompt: Which of these belong in an agent's own budget? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: A step limit
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A token budget per run, summed from usage
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A time budget for the person waiting
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The provider's context window
choices.why: That is the provider's limit, not the agent's.

prompt: How should a run that hits its budget end?

choices.text: Silently, with whatever text the model had written so far
choices.why: A limit that only truncates hides the problem it found.

choices.text: By raising the budget and continuing until the model finishes the answer
choices.why: Then it was not a budget.

choices.text: With a reason, a message, and a handoff to a person
choices.why: Right. Like lesson 7's stuck runs.

choices.text: By retrying
choices.why: A retry spends more of what ran out.
